name: West Pharmaceutical Services, Inc. (NYSE: WST)
analyst_actions: 2026-07-24 | Bank of America Securities | reiterate Buy | $410 -> $410
product: Injectable drug containment and delivery: High-Value Product elastomer components, HVP delivery devices such as SmartDose and the Synchrony S1 prefillable syringe system, Standard Products, and West Vantage services, plus licensed Daikyo Crystal Zenith polymer technology. Over 10,000 team members across 50 sites including 26 manufacturing facilities, with FY2025 net sales of $3.07B.
demand: Demand is strong and concentrated in biologics and GLP-1. Q2 2026 HVP Components rose 19.4 pct and HVP Delivery Devices 29.6 pct, and West expanded its Dublin facility (announced Mar 31, 2026) to support high-volume injectable therapies including diabetes and obesity. Standard Products and West Vantage grew only about 2 pct.
pricing_power: Not disclosed explicitly. Evidence points to mix rather than price: Q2 2026 gross margin rose to 37.7 pct from 35.7 pct and adjusted operating margin to 22.6 pct from 20.3 pct, which management attributes to a favorable mix shift from HVP upgrades including Annex 1. No price-increase disclosure was found.
competition: Not found. The company documents read do not name competitors or quantify market share. West describes itself as a leading provider of injectable solutions and a trusted partner to established and emerging drug developers. The AbbVie SmartDose 3.5mL transaction shows customers can in-source delivery-device manufacturing, which is a competitive signal.
team: Michel Lagarde became President and CEO and a director on August 31, 2026, succeeding Eric M. Green, who retired as President, CEO and Board Chair that day; Lead Independent Director Robert F. Friel became Board Chair. Lagarde was most recently Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer at Thermo Fisher Scientific and formerly Patheon COO. John Sweeney is VP Investor Relations.
market_strategy: Shift the mix toward higher-value proprietary products (Annex 1 upgrades, Biologics, GLP-1 elastomers), divest non-core delivery-device rights (SmartDose 3.5mL to AbbVie, completed Jul 1, 2026), expand capacity such as the Dublin facility, and return capital via a $0.22 quarterly dividend and $454.3M of H1 2026 share repurchases at a $258.03 average price.
bull: Q2 2026 net sales $872.3M up 13.8 pct and adjusted EPS $2.37 up 28.8 pct, FY26 guidance raised; HVP Components +19.4 pct and Delivery Devices +29.6 pct on biologics and GLP-1 mix, gross margin up to 37.7 pct.
bear: Q3 2026 guide implies reported growth slowing to 1.9-3.8 pct; Standard Products +0.7 pct organic, West Vantage gross profit fell to $21.2M; SmartDose divestiture flatters organic; May 2026 cyberattack unresolved; shares near 42x FY26 EPS.
falsifier: Q3 2026 reported net sales growth below 1.9 pct year over year, or an FY26 guidance cut, disclosed on the Q3 2026 earnings date.
web_what_changed: Q2 2026 (reported Jul 23, 2026): net sales $872.3M up 13.8 pct, adjusted diluted EPS $2.37 up 28.8 pct; FY26 guidance raised to $3.345-3.380B sales and $8.85-9.05 adjusted EPS. Jul 1, 2026 completed SmartDose 3.5mL sale to AbbVie. Jul 21, 2026 dividend $0.22 declared. Aug 31, 2026 Michel Lagarde became CEO, Eric Green retired, Robert Friel Board Chair.
web_not_known_yesterday: Not found. No company filing, press release or IR item dated 2026-09-24 or 2026-09-25 was located. The most recent primary items remain the Aug 26, 2026 investor-conference notice and the Aug 31, 2026 CEO transition; the IR events page states no upcoming event.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Mix and volume, not price. Q2 2026 HVP Components $424.1M up 19.4 pct (18.4 pct organic) and HVP Delivery Devices $131.2M up 29.6 pct, driven by Biologics strength, favorable HVP upgrade mix including Annex 1, and GLP-1 elastomer growth. Standard Products plus 2.4 pct, West Vantage plus 2.0 pct. No explicit price disclosure found.
web_suppliers: Not found. West does not disclose key suppliers in the documents read. Daikyo Seiko, Ltd is a technology licensor (Daikyo Crystal Zenith technologies) per the Q2 2026 earnings release trademark note. EDGAR full-text search of West 10-Qs for the term concentration returned no recent supplier-concentration disclosure, so constraint status is unknown.
web_customers: Not found; no customer-concentration disclosure was located in recent 10-Q or 10-K filings via EDGAR full-text search. Customers are pharmaceutical and biotechnology drug developers; West ships over 41 billion components and devices annually. AbbVie is named as the buyer of SmartDose 3.5mL manufacturing and supply rights (agreement Jan 12, 2026, completed Jul 1, 2026).
web_who_loses: Named in the sources read: West gives up the SmartDose 3.5mL revenue stream (about $55M in H2 2025 and $30M in Q3 2025), now excluded from organic growth. AbbVie gains by taking in the manufacturing and supply rights for that device. Competing injectable-component and delivery-device suppliers are not named in the documents read.
web_contradicting_evidence: Q3 2026 guidance implies reported growth decelerating to 1.9-3.8 pct from 13.8 pct, with about a 1 point FX headwind. Standard Products grew only 0.7 pct organic and West Vantage gross profit fell to $21.2M from $25.6M. Excluding SmartDose 3.5mL from organic growth flatters comparisons. The May 2026 cyberattack exfiltrated data and encrypted systems, with the investigation ongoing. Shares trade near 42x FY26 adjusted EPS.
web_if_management_right: FY26 net sales reach $3.345-3.380B, up 10-11 pct organic, and adjusted diluted EPS $8.85-9.05, as HVP mix, Annex 1 upgrades, Biologics and GLP-1 elastomers keep lifting margins. Consensus FY26 revenue is about $3.37B and EPS $8.96 from 17 analysts with a $405.38 mean target, which is consistent with management guidance.
web_if_management_wrong: Reported growth stays near the 1.9-3.8 pct Q3 guide, Standard Products and West Vantage remain flat, and HVP mix or GLP-1 demand stalls, forcing an FY26 guidance cut. With the stock near 42x forward adjusted EPS and the lowest published target at $340, the multiple de-rates first, amplified by FX headwinds and ongoing cyber-incident costs.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: AbbVie, which acquired the SmartDose 3.5mL manufacturing and supply rights (completed Jul 1, 2026). Daikyo Seiko, the Crystal Zenith technology licensor. Pharmaceutical and biotechnology customers gaining injectable capacity for biologics and for diabetes and obesity therapies, plus the wider fill-finish, elastomer and container supply chain. Other beneficiaries are not named in the sources read.
